hypotheses.justification: `convolution M B u v n = ∑ i ∈ range (M+1), ∑ j ∈ range (M+1), if i+j=n then B (u i) (v j) else 0` (FiniteGradeAlgebra.lean:41). The proof only uses hMp to rewrite with `convolution_eq_range`. Instead, unfold `convolution` and compare term by term: `sum_congr rfl` twice, then `split_ifs`. For a term with i+j=p: if i=0, then `hu 0 hp` and `hu0` give u' 0 = u 0 = 0, so both sides are `B 0 _ = 0` (`map_zero`, `LinearMap.zero_apply`). If j=0, the same argument applies with `map_zero` in the second argument. Otherwise i,j ≥ 1, so i = p-j < p and j < p, and `hu i`, `hu j` rewrite u' to u. No relation between p and M is used. In particular, when p > M every term with i+j=p already has i,j ≥ 1, and when p > 2M both sides are 0. So the statement remains true and provable without hMp.
